simple.meaning: יָהַד (yâhad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to Judaize , i.e. become Jewish.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Esther, beginning at Esther 8:17. The surrounding contexts include commandment, kingship, city, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָהַד (H3054) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָהַד (yâhad) / H3054 is traced through Esther 8:17 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3054. yahad [ יהד ] verb see below יִהוּדָה below [ יהד ] verbdenominative Hithpa`el become a Jew — only participle מִתְיַהֲדִים Est 8:17 many of the people of the land were becoming Jews.
definitions.rootNote: denominative from a form corresponding to 3061 ;

occurrences.englishText: In every province, and in every city, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had gladness, joy, a feast, and a good day. Many from among the peoples of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews was fallen on them.
